dedupe_keys.name: itu broadband maps interactive terrestrial transmission maps

description: The ITU Broadband Maps, first launched as the Interactive Terrestrial Transmission Maps, map the world's core terrestrial transmission networks, above all optical fibre backbones, together with indicators of broadband supply, to help close connectivity gaps and plan affordability and resilience strategies. The project began with a scoping exercise in December 2011 that digitised the networks of 19 operators in 13 countries from public information, over 1,000 fibre links and nodes totalling some 186,658 route kilometres, and its framework and methodology of March 2013 set out the research of core networks for the Arab, CIS, Asia-Pacific, North American, Latin American and Caribbean and African regions, with operators and administrations asked through ITU circular letters and requests for information to supply and then validate the data before publication. The web map shows layers such as the presence of optical fibre networks and indicators derived from them; ITU says the map was updated in 2025 with more analysis features, multi-layer data integration and a chatbot, and it offers a validation framework and user guide. Coverage: world, by ITU region, from 2012 onward. Format and access: interactive web map at bbmaps.itu.int, free to view, with methodology PDF; data are shown on the map, not offered as downloads. Caveats: completeness depends on what operators and administrations supply and validate; route geometry is schematic; no bulk download was found. Simulation uses: national and cross-border backbone topology for network flow and failure studies, gaps in route diversity, and planning of resilient connectivity. Related records: TeleGeography's submarine cable map covers the sea links, and the ITU ICT statistics give the demand side.
